newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, Jinro falls to its limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, Jinro falls to its limit.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Tuesday in volatile trading as profit taking set in after three days of increases, brokers said.
"The market needed a consolidation," said Chang Keun-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
The composite index ended 2.81 points lower at 701.39.
"Resistance at the 700 level was stronger than expected," Chang said. The market was forecast to fluctuate around the level for the time being.
Jinro Ltd shares dropped 800 won to its daily limit of 10,200 on news of the group's financial troubles.
Jinro, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, said it would raise a total of 1.2 trillion won by the end of 1998 to bring its equity-to-asset ratio to 24.7 percent from the current 4.43 percent.

An official at the Commercial Bank of Korea, Jinro's prime creditor, said the bank would consider fresh loans to Jinro if the group presented an acceptable restructuring plan. He would not discuss details.
Volume totalled 46.72 million shares, compared with 43.25 million on Monday.
Decliners outpaced losers 491 to 298 with 119 unchanged.
Hyundai Motor rose 500 won to 23,300 despite its announcement it had cut production at some assembly lines by four hours a day.
The company said it had reduced production of its once-best selling Sonata, Marcia and Avante by a combined 300 units a day from Monday.
Brokers said overall sentiment remained strong because of rising customer deposits with securities houses.
The deposits were estimated at 3.1 trillion won, compared with 3.06 trillion on Monday.
